reflection_oracle_classification: I classified the oracle by inspecting mask_q0_to_qn before constructing the circuit. Because every mask bit is 0, f(x) does not depend on the input, so the oracle is constant. The output_offset is 0 here; even if it were 1, it would only flip the constant output value and would not change the constant/balanced classification.
reflection_bit_order: The measurement map is reversed: q[0] is measured into c[2], q[1] into c[1], and q[2] into c[0]. Qiskit displays counts in c[n-1]...c[0] order, while the mask is written in q[0]...q[n-1] order, so a non-symmetric bit pattern can appear reversed. For this constant oracle the logical result is 000, so the reversal still displays 000.
reflection_hardware_noise: I did not run the optional IBM hardware section. On real hardware I would expect some shots to move away from the ideal 000 result because of gate errors, decoherence, and measurement/readout errors. The expected bitstring should still tend to be prominent on a sufficiently good backend, but unlike the ideal simulator the counts would usually be spread across multiple bitstrings.
